budget_items.topic: Police traffic car and K9 car (FY25 capital, now in service)
budget_items.what_was_said: The traffic car came in on schedule and on budget with money left over; the K9 car saved money because an Explorer hybrid was bought instead of an unavailable Expedition.

budget_items.topic: Hybrid cruiser battery failures / FY27 cruiser fuel type
budget_items.what_was_said: Three hybrid cruiser batteries failed this year; the chief proposed switching patrol cruisers to gas EcoBoost Explorers while keeping hybrids for single-use vehicles, citing battery replacement cost and a price gap between hybrid and gas.

budget_items.topic: Taser (Axon) replacement, FY28
budget_items.what_was_said: Old tasers lose Axon support/liability coverage in 2029; a 5-year no-interest payment program covering batteries, software and repairs was quoted, versus paying the full cost upfront. The chair raised concern about obligating multi-year capital funds and the town manager explained financing options.

budget_items.topic: Primary school site improvements (driveway/parking + playground), FY27
budget_items.what_was_said: The school department requested funding for a driveway/parking expansion and playground replacement, citing safety and access issues; the committee questioned whether project costs should be requested before design studies are complete.

budget_items.topic: Primary school driveway/parking study and expansion
budget_items.what_was_said: A feasibility study and driveway/parking expansion were priced separately; the town manager and facilities director both suggested the playground estimate is likely too low.

budget_items.topic: Primary school playground replacement
budget_items.what_was_said: Design services and new, smaller ADA/inclusive playground equipment were estimated; the town manager said a comparable rubber-surfaced playground could run far higher, and the facilities director cited an outside quote for surfacing alone plus a rough total.

budget_items.topic: Primary school window safety film
budget_items.what_was_said: Window film to reduce cooling costs and UV/impact resistance was requested as the last school to receive it; committee members pressed for actual (not "up to") savings data before ranking it.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill hot water tank replacement
budget_items.what_was_said: The nearly 20-year-old tank is beyond useful life and needs replacement.

budget_items.topic: New security camera server
budget_items.what_was_said: A redundant server would preserve camera access during an outage or cyber incident.

budget_items.topic: Primary school generator, FY28
budget_items.what_was_said: Two competing quotes were presented for a generator to protect the building during outages; committee members noted this line item's estimate has fluctuated wildly for years and said it will not be appropriated without a reliable quote.

budget_items.topic: Primary school gas condensing boilers, FY29
budget_items.what_was_said: Aging boilers are failing intermittently; a replacement quote was obtained close to the budgeted estimate.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill window replacement design/architectural plan, FY30
budget_items.what_was_said: Original single-pane windows need a full architectural replacement plan; may later qualify for MSBA accelerated repair funding if Turkey Hill remains a school 25-30 years.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill complete window replacement, FY31
budget_items.what_was_said: Full window replacement was estimated, potentially offset by MSBA accelerated repair program funding; the figure was called an older estimate likely to rise.

budget_items.topic: Middle high school projector replacement, FY31
budget_items.what_was_said: Aging wall-mounted projectors need replacement; committee suggested flat-screen displays may be more current technology by then.

budget_items.topic: Network firewall replacement, FY32
budget_items.what_was_said: The current firewall reaches end of life in FY30; a figure was given for the cost of restoring service after a cyberattack, and a member urged a joint town/school security review before this priority slips further.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill renovation or new build, FY32
budget_items.what_was_said: The plan flags an eventual full renovation or rebuild of Turkey Hill without a cost yet, pending a district decision on the building's future.

budget_items.topic: Turkey Hill comprehensive building assessment (prior study)
budget_items.what_was_said: A prior ARPA-funded study estimated the base cost to bring Turkey Hill up to code, not counting further modernization for elementary programming.

budget_items.topic: Track and field project (turf, track, retaining walls)
budget_items.what_was_said: Committee members debated whether a rough prior estimate is reliable without completed engineering and bid documents, warning against seeking town meeting authorization for a figure that could be far higher; part of the funding was floated as coming through a separate warrant article and inside borrowing capacity.

budget_items.topic: FY23 primary school hazardous abatement / capital accounting error
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager found this FY23 line still showing an available balance though the funds had actually been transferred to the TCP roof project at a prior town meeting and never closed out; she is holding back FY26 spending until this is corrected at May town meeting.

budget_items.topic: FY26 total capital appropriation
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager stated the total capital approved for FY26 while explaining she is withholding a portion pending the accounting correction.

budget_items.topic: FY22 Ritter Elementary ADA ramp construction appropriation
budget_items.what_was_said: This older appropriation still exists and was not needed as a standalone project since it would roll into a municipal building redesign; the town manager plans to propose splitting it between project estimators and a stormwater utility study at fall special town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Free cash certification status
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager reported ongoing turnover in the accounting office means free cash has not been certified and she cannot yet estimate funding availability for capital.

decisions.decision: Chair and town manager agreed to aim for a prioritized capital recommendation by year-end, but to allow slipping into January if needed rather than rushing.
Committee agreed to proceed with reviewing the school capital plan tonight even though the track and field project is not yet fully scoped, with the option to revisit it later.
Facilities director asked to research and report back actual (not "up to") energy/cost savings data for the window safety film before it is ranked.
Committee asked that future capital line items state the basis and date of any cost estimate or quote.
Committee asked the school district to compile a digital, centralized list of known building deficiencies/looming capital needs instead of relying on institutional memory.
Chair and superintendent agreed the district needs to land on a track and field plan by spring 2026, given safety urgency.
Committee floated doing engineering/bid documents for the track and field project in the spring and seeking the remaining construction funding at a fall special town meeting.
Meeting schedule set: DPW and fire department next week (in person if possible), facilities the following week, roughly three consecutive Wednesdays.
Chair agreed to explore inviting a non-voting finance committee member to sit in on capital planning meetings while one member is traveling.
Fiscal policy review pushed to a future in-person meeting rather than tackled tonight.

minutes.headline: Town manager found a capital fund already spent but never closed on the books, needing a town meeting fix
minutes.summary: The Capital Planning Committee heard FY27-FY37 capital requests from the police department (cruisers, hybrid-vs-gas fleet decisions, taser financing) and the school district (primary school driveway/playground, Turkey Hill repairs, technology, and an urgent, still-unscoped track and field project). The town manager reported free cash is not yet certified due to accounting office turnover, and disclosed she found a prior-year capital appropriation that had already been transferred to another project but never closed out on the books across two town meetings, which she is now moving to correct at May town meeting.

what_happened.line: The town manager disclosed a prior-year capital appropriation was spent and shifted to another project but never closed out on the books across two town meetings, and said she will seek a fix at May town meeting.
Police and school officials presented FY27-FY37 capital requests, including cruiser fleet fuel-type choices, taser financing, and primary school and Turkey Hill building repairs.

The school district's track and field project remains unscoped, but the committee agreed to keep reviewing the rest of the school capital plan and asked the district to settle a track and field plan by spring 2026.
The committee set a near-weekly meeting schedule, taking up DPW and fire department requests next, and asked that future capital line items state the basis and date of any cost estimate.

why_it_matters: The unresolved capital fund transfer will need a town meeting article in May to close it out on the books, which residents will be asked to vote on.
This year's capital requests -- police cruisers and tasers, and school driveway, playground, generator and boiler work -- feed the prioritized list the committee plans to send to town meeting.
A safety-driven push to fix the district's track and field, still unscoped, could mean a separate funding request as soon as a fall special town meeting.
